input.prompt:
In this Next.js + Mantine codebase (/Volumes/Development/next-www-toastboy), I'm working on SYS-599: sweep the codebase for components/pages that return a wrapper element (Container, Paper, Box, div, etc.) purely to satisfy JSX's single-root-element requirement or to group children, with NO real layout/sizing/styling/props doing actual work. These should be replaced with a Fragment (`<>...</>`), or with `Center` (or another correct semantic Mantine primitive) where the actual intent is pure centering/alignment with no width/sizing constraint.

Already fixed as reference example (do not re-flag): SignIn's loading branch, which used to wrap `<Loader />` in a bare `<Container>` and was changed to `<Center>`.

Please search:
1. All files under src/components/**/*.tsx
2. All files under src/app/**/page.tsx and layout.tsx

For each, look for JSX return statements (or the top-level return of the component) that use `<Container>`, `<Paper>`, `<Box>`, `<div>`, `<Stack>`, `<Group>` or similar Mantine/HTML wrapper elements as the outermost/root element, where:
- The wrapper has no props at all (or only trivial ones that don't affect layout, e.g. just a `key`), OR
- The wrapper has props like `size`, `p`, `m`, `w`, `bg`, `shadow`, `withBorder` etc. that ARE doing real work (these should NOT be flagged — only flag truly unnecessary ones)
- The wrapper's only purpose seems to be providing a single root JSX element for a component/page that renders one or more children

Be careful to distinguish:
- Legitimate uses of Container/Paper/Box/Stack/Group (real width capping, padding, background, spacing, borders, semantic grouping) — DO NOT flag these
- Wrappers used purely for JSX single-root satisfaction with zero styling purpose — DO flag these
- Cases where centering is the real intent but the wrong primitive (e.g. Container instead of Center) is used — flag these separately as "should be Center"

For each finding, report:
- File path
- Line number
- The current wrapper element and its props (or lack thereof)
- Whether it should become a Fragment `<>...</>` or `Center` (or other primitive)
- A one-line justification

Report back a concise list of findings, grouped by file, with file:line references. Do not make any edits — this is research only. Aim to be thorough — check every file under src/components and src/app, not just a sample.

<result>Based on a full sweep of `src/components/**/*.tsx` and `src/app/**/{page,layout}.tsx`, here are the findings.

## Findings

### src/components/AdminUserList/AdminUserList.tsx:117-121
```tsx
return (
    <Container>
        <Text c="red">{errorMessage}</Text>
    </Container>
);
```
- Wrapper: `<Container>` with zero props, wraps a single `<Text>` child (early-return error branch).
- Recommendation: **Fragment** (`<>...</>`). No width capping/centering is being used — the child is a single, non-centered text node, so `Container`'s theme sizing is pure noise here.

### src/components/TableIndexList/TableIndexList.tsx:31-41
```tsx
export const TableIndexList = () => (
    <Paper>
        <List>...</List>
    </Paper>
);
```
- Wrapper: root return, `<Paper>` with zero props, wraps a single `<List>` child.
- Recommendation: **Fragment**. `Paper` contributes no shadow/border/padding/background here; it's purely satisfying the single-root requirement.

### src/app/footy/countrymap/page.tsx:21-36
```tsx
return (
    <Paper>
        <Title order={2} mb="md">Toastboy FC World Map</Title>
        <Text mb="md">...</Text>
        <PlayerCountryMap countries={countries} />
    </Paper>
);
```
- Wrapper: page root, `<Paper>` with zero props, grouping three children.
- Recommendation: **Fragment**. No padding/shadow/border is applied, so `Paper` isn't providing a card surface — just grouping.

### src/app/footy/response/page.tsx:34-39 and 46-51 (two occurrences)
```tsx
return (
    <Box>
        <Text>{errorMessage}</Text>
        <Anchor href="/footy/game">Go to the game page</Anchor>
    </Box>
);
```
(and the near-identical block at 46-51 for "Invitation details are missing.")
- Wrapper: `<Box>` with zero props, grouping a `Text` + `Anchor` pair, in two separate early-return error branches.
- Recommendation: **Fragment** for both. No styling/layout props at all; `Box` here is only satisfying JSX's single-root rule.

### src/app/footy/admin/page.tsx:24-37 (secondary/nested finding)
```tsx
<Paper>
    <Flex mb="lg" gap="md" wrap="wrap" justify="center">
        <AdminUpdatePlayerRecords .../>
        <AdminExportAuth .../>
    </Flex>
</Paper>
```
- Wrapper: `<Paper>` with zero props, nested inside the (legitimately-styled) root `Container`, wrapping a *single* `<Flex>` child that already does the real layout work (gap/wrap/justify).
- Recommendation: **Fragment**. Since `Flex` is already a single valid JSX child, `Paper` here isn't even needed for the single-root rule — it does no visual work (no shadow/border/padding) and could be removed entirely.
- Lower confidence than the above since `Paper` is used elsewhere in the codebase as a deliberate "card" convention, but here it wraps only one child and applies no styling, so it reads as leftover scaffolding.

### src/components/PlayerProfile/PlayerProfile.tsx:178-189 (secondary/nested finding, lower confidence)
```tsx
<Group>
    <Paper p="sm" w="auto" style={{ flex: '1' }}>
        <PlayerHeatmap data={history} year={year} />
    </Paper>
</Group>
```
- Wrapper: `<Group>` with zero props, wraps a single `<Paper>` child (which itself has real props).
- Recommendation: **Fragment**. `Group`'s row-layout/gap behavior is irrelevant with only one child; it's not doing any grouping work. Flag with lower confidence — could be intentional scaffolding for a future second item, worth confirming with the author before removing.

## Not flagged (checked, but legitimate)

For completeness, these were inspected because they use bare/props-light `Container`/`Paper`/`Box`/`Stack`/`Group`, but were judged to be doing real work and are **not** flagged:
- `CustomAppShell.tsx:56` — bare `<Container>` in the header; Mantine `Container` without `fluid`/`size` still applies a real default max-width + centering, and here it's plausibly matching the width of `AppShell.Main`'s `Container size="xl"` for visual alignment.
- All the `Stack`/`Group`/`Flex` usages with 2+ children found via the bare-tag grep (`DeleteAccountForm`, `PasswordResetForm`, `EnquiryForm`, `NewPlayerForm`, `PasswordChangeForm`, `SignIn`, `ClaimSignup`, `UserButton`, `PlayerProfileForm`, `not-found.tsx`, `books/page.tsx`) — these rely on `Stack`'s default gap or `Group`'s default row-flow to lay out multiple real children, which is genuine layout work, not single-root padding.
- `NewGameForm.tsx:104` bare `<Paper>` wrapping `Title` + form `Box` — consistent with the repo-wide "Paper as form card" convention used across dozens of forms (`ClaimSignup`, `ForgottenPasswordForm`, `GameInvitationResponseForm`, `PasswordResetForm`, `SignIn`, etc.), all with multiple children, so treated as intentional design language rather than filler.
- Every `Container`/`Paper`/`Box`/`Flex`/`Stack` root wrapper elsewhere carries real sizing/spacing/ref/className/`component="form"` props (e.g. `AdminPlayerList`, `DrinkersForm`, `PickerForm`, `MoneyForm`, `ResponsesForm`, `PlayerList`, `PlayerCard`, `PlayerInfo`, `RecordsTable`, `Turnout`, `WinnersTable`, `YearTable`, `GameDaySummary`, `FamilyTree`, `PlayerCountryMap`, `MoneyChart`, `PieChart`, `PlayerHeatmap`, `DebugFontSizes`, `DebugBreakpoints`, `DebugSizeOverlay`, `NavBarNested`, `docs/layout.tsx`).
- `SignIn.tsx:94-97` — already fixed reference example (`<Center><Loader/></Center>`), confirmed present and correct, not re-flagged.
- All redirect-only page/layout components (`fixtures/[year]`, `results/[year]`, `table/[table]/[year]`, `winners/[year]`, `game/page.tsx`, `drinkers/page.tsx`, `admin/layout.tsx`, `(authenticated)/layout.tsx`, root `page.tsx`) return `null`/`children`/nothing JSX-wrapper related.</result>

# Run the project's mandatory finalisation checklist before reporting any task as done

## Steps

1. Run `npm run typecheck` and capture all output.
2. Run `npm run lint` and capture all output.
3. Run `npx knip` and capture all output.
4. If any of the three produced errors or warnings:
   - For lint issues — run `npm run lint:fix` first to auto-fix what it can, then re-run `npm run lint` to see what remains.
   - For knip findings — remove the unused files, exports, or dependencies it reports.
   - Fix **every** remaining issue — do not skip, suppress, or dismiss any output.
   - If you are unsure whether a problem existed before your changes, run `git stash`, repeat all three commands to establish a pre-change baseline, then `git stash pop` and fix only the new issues.
   - After fixing, re-run all three commands to confirm they are clean.
5. Repeat until all three commands exit with code 0 and report no errors or warnings.

## Done criterion

`npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npx knip` all exit with code 0 and report no errors or warnings. Only then report the task as complete.

## Notes

- Fix issues in the order they appear — later errors are often caused by earlier ones.
- Avoid silencing a lint rule or adding a `@ts-ignore` / `eslint-disable` comment to make the output go away — fix the underlying problem. If a suppression is truly necessary (false positive, required vendor API), scope it as narrowly as possible (single line, specific rule) and add a short inline comment explaining why.
- If a typecheck error is in a generated file (`prisma/generated/`, `prisma/zod/`), do not edit it — regenerate it with `npx prisma generate` instead.

- `AdminUserList.tsx` — dropped bare `Container` around a single `Text` error message
- `TableIndexList.tsx` — dropped bare `Paper` around a single `List`
- `footy/countrymap/page.tsx` — bare `Paper` → Fragment (3 real children)
- `footy/response/page.tsx` — two bare `Box` wrappers → Fragments (each wrapping `Text` + `Anchor`)
- `footy/admin/page.tsx` — dropped bare `Paper` that wrapped a single `Flex` already doing the real layout work
- `PlayerProfile.tsx` — dropped bare `Group` that wrapped a single `Paper` already doing the real styling work

The `SignIn` component mentioned in the ticket (Container → Center for the loading spinner) was already fixed, confirming your hunch that some ground had been covered since the ticket was written. I also checked `CustomAppShell`'s bare `Container` and all the `Paper`-as-form-card usages across the codebase — those are doing genuine work (default max-width/centering, or the established form-card convention) and were correctly left alone.

Verified clean: `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `knip`, plus full page and component test suites (702 + 235 tests) all pass. Changes are unstaged for your review — let me know if you'd like me to commit.
